nodes.label: Medical Scribe
nodes.desc: Documents provider-patient encounters in real time into the EHR.

nodes.label: HIPAA
nodes.desc: Federal law protecting patient health information privacy and security.

nodes.label: PHI
nodes.desc: Protected Health Information — any identifiable health data.

nodes.label: Minimum Necessary
nodes.desc: Access only the PHI needed to do your job.

nodes.label: Medical Terminology
nodes.desc: Greek/Latin-based language of medicine: prefixes, roots, suffixes.

nodes.label: Anatomy & Planes
nodes.desc: Directional terms (superior, proximal) and body planes.

nodes.label: Abdominal Regions
nodes.desc: 9 regions / 4 quadrants used to localize abdominal pain.

nodes.label: Skeletal Landmarks
nodes.desc: Bones and palpable landmarks documented in exams.

nodes.label: SOAP Note
nodes.desc: Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan — standard note structure.

nodes.label: Chief Complaint
nodes.desc: Why the patient came, ideally in quotes.

nodes.label: HPI
nodes.desc: Narrative of present illness: onset, location, duration, character, aggravating/relieving, timing, severity.

nodes.label: Review of Systems
nodes.desc: Head-to-toe symptom checklist beyond the HPI.

nodes.label: PMHx / Meds / Allergies
nodes.desc: Past history, medications, allergies — semi-subjective context.

nodes.label: Golden Rules
nodes.desc: Document what is said/done; never fabricate or interpret.

nodes.label: Vital Signs
nodes.desc: BP, HR, RR, temp, SpO2, pain score — objective baseline.

nodes.label: Physical Exam
nodes.desc: Provider's observed findings by system; pediatric vs adult norms differ.

nodes.label: Clinical Course
nodes.desc: What happened during the stay: interventions, response.

nodes.label: Results Review
nodes.desc: Labs/imaging and provider interpretation of them.

nodes.label: Assessment & Plan
nodes.desc: Diagnosis reasoning and management per problem.

nodes.label: Clinical Decision Making
nodes.desc: Risk, data reviewed, alternatives considered — drives billing level.

nodes.label: ICD-10 Coding
nodes.desc: Diagnosis codes that must be supported by documentation.

nodes.label: Addenda & Corrections
nodes.desc: Late changes are addenda with reason and author — never delete.

nodes.label: Primary Care Clinic
nodes.desc: Preventive medicine, chronic disease, wellness visits.

nodes.label: Annual Physical (AWV)
nodes.desc: Preventive visit: screening, immunizations, counseling.

nodes.label: Prenatal Care
nodes.desc: Pregnancy tracking: dates, fundal height, fetal heart tones.

nodes.label: Well Child Checks
nodes.desc: Pediatric milestones, growth curves, vaccines.

nodes.label: Chronic Disease Mgmt
nodes.desc: Diabetes, HTN, asthma: control status and med adjustments.

nodes.label: Emergency Department
nodes.desc: Acute care: triage, resuscitation, disposition.

nodes.label: Triage & ESI
nodes.desc: Severity indexing driving wait order.

nodes.label: Chest Pain Workup
nodes.desc: ECG within 10 min, troponin, rule out ACS.

nodes.label: ED Abdominal Pain
nodes.desc: Differential broad: appendicitis, stones, ectopic.

nodes.label: Stroke / CVA
nodes.desc: Time-critical: last known well, NIHSS, tPA window.

nodes.label: ED Medications
nodes.desc: Common acute meds and documentation of response.

nodes.label: E/M Levels
nodes.desc: 99202-99215 outpatient, 99281-99288 ED levels.

nodes.label: Billing by Time
nodes.desc: Total time can determine level since 2021 rules.

nodes.label: Critical Care Time
nodes.desc: ≥30 min continuous high-intensity care, separately billed.

nodes.label: Medical Necessity
nodes.desc: Services justified by symptoms/findings — documented rationale.

nodes.label: Quality Measures
nodes.desc: CMS/TJC core measures tied to reimbursement.

nodes.label: Medicolegal Record
nodes.desc: The chart is a legal document: contemporaneous, factual.

nodes.label: Note vs Chart
nodes.desc: One visit note lives inside the lifelong longitudinal chart.

nodes.label: Future Readers
nodes.desc: Write for consultants, lawyers, patients reading later.

glossary.SOAP: Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan — the standard medical note format.
glossary.HPI: History of Present Illness — narrative of the current complaint (OLDCARTS).
glossary.ROS: Review of Systems — head-to-toe inventory of positive/negative symptoms.
glossary.CC: Chief Complaint — the primary reason for the encounter, often in patient's words.
glossary.PHI: Protected Health Information — individually identifiable health data under HIPAA.
glossary.ICD-10: International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision — diagnosis coding system.
glossary.E/M: Evaluation and Management — billing category for office/ED visits (e.g., 99213).
glossary.MDM: Medical Decision Making — complexity of problems, data, and risk; sets E/M level.
glossary.CDM: Clinical Decision Making — same concept as MDM; documented reasoning.
glossary.AWV: Annual Wellness Visit — Medicare preventive visit with screening plan.
glossary.WCC: Well Child Check — scheduled pediatric preventive visit.
glossary.VS: Vital Signs — BP, pulse, respirations, temperature, oxygen saturation.
glossary.ED: Emergency Department — acute care setting; also 'estimated date' in obstetrics.
glossary.ACS: Acute Coronary Syndrome — heart attack/unstable angina spectrum.
glossary.NIHSS: National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale — stroke severity score.
glossary.tPA: Tissue plasminogen activator — clot-busting drug for ischemic stroke.
glossary.ESI: Emergency Severity Index — 5-level triage acuity scale.
glossary.Addendum: A later addition to a note, signed, dated, with reason; never erases originals.
glossary.OLDCARTS: Onset, Location, Duration, Character, Aggravating/Relieving, Timing, Severity — HPI elements.
glossary.Quadrants: Four divisions of the abdomen (RUQ, LUQ, RLQ, LLQ) for pain localization.
glossary.Proximal: Closer to the trunk or point of attachment (opposite of distal).
glossary.Distal: Farther from the trunk or point of attachment.
glossary.Tachycardia: Heart rate over 100 bpm in adults.
glossary.Bradycardia: Heart rate under 60 bpm in adults.
glossary.Dyspnea: Shortness of breath or labored breathing.
glossary.Differential: List of plausible diagnoses considered before concluding.
glossary.Disposition: Where the patient goes after the ED visit (home, admit, transfer).
glossary.Co-sign: Provider signature validating the scribe-documented note.

flashcards.back: Onset, Location, Duration, Character, Aggravating/Relieving factors, Timing, Severity.
Protected Health Information — any individually identifiable health data governed by HIPAA.

flashcards.front: Rule of thumb for scribe corrections after signing?
flashcards.back: Never delete — write an addendum that is dated, timed, attributed, and states the reason.

flashcards.front: Normal adult vital ranges: BP, HR, RR, SpO2?
How many abdominal quadrants and regions?
flashcards.back: 4 quadrants (umbilical cross) or 9 regions (2 horizontal + 2 vertical lines).
Proximal = closer to trunk/attachment; distal = farther (elbow is proximal to wrist).

flashcards.front: What drives E/M level selection since 2021 (outpatient)?
flashcards.back: Medical Decision Making or total time on the date of the encounter.
At least 30 minutes of continuous, high-intensity care; independently billed.
The service must be justified by the patient's signs/symptoms/diagnosis — documented so payers accept it.

flashcards.front: Who are the future readers of a chart?
flashcards.back: Consultants, other providers, auditors/payers, lawyers, and the patient themselves.

flashcards.front: Can a scribe document that a physical exam was 'normal'?
flashcards.back: Only if the provider stated it; scribes record exactly what is said or done — never assume.

flashcards.front: What is the minimum necessary standard?
flashcards.back: Access/use/disclose only the PHI required for the task at hand.

flashcards.front: What does ICD-10 provide and who assigns it?
flashcards.back: Diagnosis codes for billing/statistics; assigned by the provider/coder and must be supported by documentation.
